account: Today I have kept my scheduled correspondence, market walk, lunch, and office business, and have now reached the dockside cottage for fifteen hundred tea. I have a general feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but little firm evidence. Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, which seems ordinary for his trade; most others had no news. The builder visited me carrying a lantern and requested a great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at eighteen hundred. He says new lanterns are installed and there is no particular problem, just a routine review of their coverage. I approved, and the secretary says she secured an appointment addendum with my appointments. This might simply be municipal business; I have not seen evidence of another purpose. The oddest detail is today's tea appointment: the book names neither the host nor a precise cottage. The secretary said dockside workers could not identify the host and asked whether I remembered an invitation, but I have received none naming anyone. I found the neighbour waiting by the cottage at (16, -60, 105) and greeted them. They have not yet answered. I cannot yet tell whether the vague tea arrangement and tomorrow's lighting inspection are connected. I should hear the neighbour out rather than assume a hidden scheme.
